solutions.latex: $f(x)=3x^{\frac52}$. After reflection in the $x$ axis: $y=-3x^{\frac52}$. After translation 3 units right: $y=-3(x-3)^{\frac52}$. After translation 4 units down: $y=-3(x-3)^{\frac52}-4$.
$f'(x)$ touches the $x$ axis at $x=-4$ without changing sign, so $f'(-4)=0$ with no change in the sign of the gradient: a horizontal point of inflexion at $x=-4$.
$f'(x)=3x^2-4$, so $f(x)=x^3-4x+c=x(x^2-4)+c=x(x+2)(x-2)+c$. This is the cubic $y=x(x+2)(x-2)$ translated vertically by $c$ units, which matches graph B.

solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct solution

Let $y=\tan x\cos x$. Product rule: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\cos x\sec^2x+\tan x(-\sin x)=\dfrac{\cos x}{\cos^2x}-\dfrac{\sin^2x}{\cos x}=\dfrac{1}{\cos x}-\dfrac{\sin^2x}{\cos x}=\dfrac{\cos^2x}{\cos x}=\cos x$.

Method 2: $y=\tan x\cos x=\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\times\cos x=\sin x$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\cos x$.

solutions.latex: $y=\ln(2x-1)-\ln(x+1)$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2}{2x-1}-\dfrac{1}{x+1}$. At $x=2$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac23-\dfrac13=\dfrac13$ (gradient of tangent). Gradient of normal $=-3$ (perpendicular lines, $m_1m_2=-1$). When $x=2$, $y=\ln\left(\dfrac33\right)=\ln1=0$. Using $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$: $y-0=-3(x-2)$, so $y=-3x+6$ is the equation of the normal.

solutions.latex:
Stationary points occur when $f'(x)=0$: $4(x-2)^2(x+1)=0$, so $x=-1,\ 2$. $f(-1)=-27$ and $f(2)=0$, so the stationary points are $(-1,-27)$ and $(2,0)$.

Nature: $f''(-1)=12(-1)(-3)=36>0$, concave up, so $(-1,-27)$ is a minimum turning point. $f''(2)=12(2)(0)=0$, so there is a possible horizontal inflexion at $x=2$. Testing concavity:

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 1.5 & 2 & 2.5\\ \hline f''(x) & -9 & 0 & 15 \end{array}$$

The concavity changes (concave down to concave up), so $(2,0)$ is a horizontal point of inflexion.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct stationary points and justifies the nature of both correctly; 2: correct stationary points and justifies the nature of one correctly; 1: correct stationary points

solutions.latex:
$f''(x)=12x(x-2)=0$ when $x=0,\ 2$. $(2,0)$ was already established as a horizontal inflexion. Test $x=0$:

$$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & -0.5 & 0 & 0.5\\ \hline f''(x) & 15 & 0 & -9 \end{array}$$

The concavity changes, so $(0,-16)$ is a point of inflexion.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: justifies a second point of inflexion exists by testing for change in concavity; 1: obtains second possible point of inflexion

solutions.latex: The yearly growths $50,\ 50(0.9),\ 50(0.9)^2,\dots$ form a G.P. with $r=0.9$, an infinite series. $S_\infty$ exists as $|r|<1$. $S_\infty=\dfrac{a}{1-r}=\dfrac{50}{1-0.9}=500$ cm. So the limiting growth is 500 cm and the limiting height is $80+500=580\text{ cm}<600\text{ cm}$. Therefore the tree will never reach a height of 6 m.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct solution (calculates $S_\infty$ correctly, adds the 80 cm to get the limiting height and concludes correctly); 1: identifies $S_\infty$ needs to be calculated and calculates it correctly

solutions.latex: To reach a height of 5 m the tree needs to grow $420$ cm. $S_n=\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}$: $420=\dfrac{50(1-0.9^n)}{1-0.9}$, so $42=50(1-0.9^n)$, $\dfrac{42}{50}=1-0.9^n$, $0.9^n=\dfrac{8}{50}=0.16$, $n=\dfrac{\ln0.16}{\ln0.9}\approx17.39344$. The tree will reach 5 metres during the 18th year.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct solution; 1: substitutes correctly into $S_n$ for a GP
2: shows the value for both $C_0$ and $k$ correctly; 1: shows the value for $C_0$ or $k$ correctly

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle HAB$: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{HB}$ and $\tan\theta=\dfrac{AB}{1}$, so $HB=\dfrac1{\cos\theta}$ and $AB=\tan\theta$. Similarly in $\triangle SDC$: $SC=\dfrac1{\cos\theta}$ and $DC=\tan\theta$.

Distance walked $=2HB=\dfrac2{\cos\theta}$, so time walked $=\dfrac2{\cos\theta}\div4=\dfrac1{2\cos\theta}$ hours.

Distance skated $=6-2\tan\theta$, so time skated $=\dfrac{6-2\tan\theta}{12}$ hours.

So $T=\dfrac1{2\cos\theta}+\dfrac{6-2\tan\theta}{12}=\dfrac1{2\cos\theta}+\dfrac12-\dfrac{\tan\theta}{6}$, as required.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: obtains, with working, correct distances travelled and times taken; 1: obtains, with working, the correct distances travelled

solutions.latex:
$T=\dfrac{(\cos\theta)^{-1}}{2}+\dfrac12-\dfrac{\tan\theta}{6}$.

$\dfrac{dT}{d\theta}=-\dfrac{(-\sin\theta)(\cos\theta)^{-2}}{2}-\dfrac{\sec^2\theta}{6}=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{2\cos^2\theta}-\dfrac1{6\cos^2\theta}=\dfrac{3\sin\theta-1}{6\cos^2\theta}$.

For minimum $T$, $\dfrac{dT}{d\theta}=0$: $3\sin\theta-1=0$ (as $\dfrac1{\cos^2\theta}=\sec^2\theta\neq0$), so $\sin\theta=\dfrac13$ and $\theta\approx19^\circ28'$.

Test with $\theta=10^\circ,\ 19^\circ28',\ 30^\circ$: the slope $\dfrac{dT}{d\theta}$ is negative, zero, positive (\ \ / shape), so there is a minimum turning point at $\theta=19^\circ28'$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: correct solution (must include testing that $\theta$ gives a minimum $T$); 3: solves correctly for $\theta$; 2: correct equation to solve for $\theta$; 1: correct use of chain rule and correct derivative of $\tan\theta$
